requirements.requirement: On node1, make the currently supplied DNS nameserver persistent and effective after restart.
requirements.summary: The supplied DHCP/runtime nameserver was directly identified as 10.100.253.1. It was stored in the active NetworkManager profile, applied successfully, and remained present in both the persistent profile and effective resolver after a reboot; live DNS resolution also recovered.

requirements.requirement: On node1, add infra.test as the persistent system search domain.
requirements.summary: infra.test was stored as the NetworkManager IPv4 DNS search domain and appeared in NetworkManager-generated /etc/resolv.conf before and after reboot.

overall_summary: Both task outcomes are satisfied. Direct pre- and post-reboot observations show that the supplied nameserver and infra.test search domain are persistent and effective. The provider-wide restart protocol for node1 is complete and internally consistent: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and bounded disruption, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered NetworkManager, connection, resolver configuration, and DNS behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The profile modification was required to persist the requested settings, the device reapply was required to activate and verify them, and the reboot was required to demonstrate persistence and satisfy the restart protocol. The reboot was acknowledged, the boot identity changed consistently with lifecycle observations, services recovered, package health remained good, no failed services appeared, and socket or temporary-file differences were normal reboot-related identity changes rather than residue.
